originalTitle: Ahead of Market: 10 things that will decide stock market action on Monday
simplifiedContent: The Indian stock market has been doing poorly for five days in a row, mainly because oil prices are high and foreign investors are taking their money out. Even though the market tried to recover a bit during the day, the overall feeling is still negative due to high interest rates in the US and uncertainty around the world. Analysts are watching certain key levels in the Nifty, a important stock market index, to see what will happen next. This will help them understand how the market will move on Monday. The market's ability to bounce back and individual stock performances will also be important to watch.

originalTitle: US Fed action, oil swings to test bullion as traders eye West Asia risks: Analysts
simplifiedContent: This week is important for the prices of gold and silver because the US Federal Reserve is going to decide whether to change interest rates. Traders are also watching oil prices closely, as well as the ongoing tensions between the US and Iran, to see how they might affect gold and silver prices. The Federal Reserve's decision and other economic announcements will have a big impact on the prices of these precious metals. This means that investors should pay attention to these events, as they could lead to big changes in the prices of gold and silver. The combination of these factors makes this a crucial week for people who invest in gold and silver.

originalTitle: GS, Nomura, Axis hired to run Carlyle’s India automotive platform IPO
simplifiedContent: Carlyle, a big investment company, is planning to sell some of its shares in an Indian company called Highway Roop Precision Technologies through a process called an Initial Public Offering (IPO). They've hired some well-known banks, including GS, Nomura, and Axis, to help manage the sale. The IPO is expected to raise around $500 million and could value the company at $2 billion. This is mainly an "offer for sale", which means Carlyle is selling some of its existing shares in the company. This matters because it allows Carlyle to make some money from its investment in the company, which makes auto parts.

originalTitle: CBDT issues crypto reporting guidelines for exchanges under Income-tax Act 2025
simplifiedContent: The government's tax department, called the CBDT, has created rules for cryptocurrency exchanges to follow when reporting information. This is part of a larger effort to share tax information internationally, which has been supported by a group of 20 major countries (the G20). These rules are important because they will help the government keep track of cryptocurrency transactions and make sure people are paying the right amount of taxes. The CBDT is doing this under a new law called the Income-tax Act 2025. This change will affect how cryptocurrency exchanges operate and report information to the government.

originalTitle: Wall St Week Ahead-US stocks face tests from Fed decision, tech-led earnings deluge
simplifiedContent: This week, the US stock market will be closely watched as two important events happen. The Federal Reserve (or "Fed") will make a decision that could affect the market, and many big technology companies will release their earnings reports. These earnings reports will show how well these companies have been doing, which can impact their stock prices. The combination of the Fed's decision and the earnings reports could be challenging for the stock market, and investors will be paying close attention to see how things play out. This is important because it could affect the overall direction of the stock market in the coming days.

originalTitle: Expert View: Mid-year - recalibrating India equity story with a positive bias, says Vinod Nair
simplifiedContent: An expert named Vinod Nair has shared his view on the Indian stock market. He thinks that the market will do well, and has a "positive bias" which means he's optimistic about its performance. He's set a target for the market to reach 29,000 by December 2027, which would be a 21% increase from now. This means he expects the market to grow significantly over the next few years. This matters because it could affect how investors decide to put their money into the Indian stock market.
